## Early life and education
Oyelowo is an _omoba_ (or prince) of the Yoruba people in the Nigerian chieftaincy system, his grandfather having been king of "a part of Oyo State called Awe". He has commented of his background: "It sounds way more impressive than it actually is. There are so many royal families in Africa",[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-ind1-8) "royal families are a dime a dozen in Nigeria";[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-:1-2) "what we think of as royalty in the UK is very different to royalty in Nigeria: if you were to throw a stone there, you would hit about 30 princes. So, it's a bit more like being the Prince of Islington: it was useful for getting dates but probably not much else."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-11)
Oyelowo attended a "military-style" boarding-school named Lagos State Model College Meiran (now Lagos State Model Junior College Meiran.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-ind1-8) His family returned to London when Oyelowo was 14,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-12) settling in Islington.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-ind1-8)
While enrolled in theatre studies at City and Islington College, his teacher suggested that he become an actor. Oyelowo enrolled for a year in an acting foundation course, at the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art (LAMDA).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-ind1-8) He finished his three-year training in 1998.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-13)
He also spent time with the National Youth Theatre.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-14)

## Early life and education
He began his stage career in 1999 when he was offered a season with the Royal Shakespeare Company playing roles in Ben Jonson's _Volpone_, as the title character in _Oroonoko_ (which he also performed in the BBC radio adaptation) and Shakespeare's_Antony and Cleopatra_ (1999) alongside Guy Henry, Frances de la Tour and Alan Bates. However, he is best known for his next stage performance as King Henry VI[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-big-10) in the Royal Shakespeare Company's 2001 productions of Shakespeare's trilogy of plays about the king as a part of its season _This England: The Histories_. In a major landmark for colour-blind casting, Oyelowo was the first black actor to play an English king in a major production of Shakespeare, and although this casting choice was initially criticised by some in the media, Oyelowo's performance was critically acclaimed and later won the 2001 Ian Charleson Award for best performance by an actor under 30 in a classical play.
In 2005, he appeared in a production of _Prometheus Bound_, which was revived in New York City in 2007. In 2006, he made his directorial debut on a production of _The White Devil_, produced by Inservice, his theatre company in Brighton which is co-run with fellow Brighton-based actors Priyanga Burford, Israel Aduramo, Penelope Cobbuld, and his wife, Jessica.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-15) He played the title role in _Othello_ in 2016 at the New York Theatre Workshop with Daniel Craig as Iago, directed by Sam Gold.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-16) In 2024, he starred in the Royal National Theatre production of Coriolanus.

## Early life and education
Oyelowo is best known for playing MI5 officer Danny Hunter in the British drama series _Spooks_ (known in North America as _MI-5_) from 2002 to 2004. He had before that appeared in _Tomorrow La Scala_ (2002), _Maisie Raine_ (1998) and _Brothers and Sisters_ (1998). Soon after the end of his time on _Spooks_ Oyelowo also appeared in the two Christmas specials of _As Time Goes By_ (2005). In 2006, he appeared in the television film _Born Equal_ alongside Nikki Amuka-Bird as a couple fleeing persecution in Nigeria – they also both appeared in _Shoot the Messenger_ (2006) and in _[The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_No.\_1\_Ladies'\_Detective\_Agency\_(TV\_series) "The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency (TV series)")_ (2008) as a husband and wife. Other cameos have included _Mayo_ (guest-starring on 30 April 2006) and the television film _Sweet Nothing in My Ear_ (2008, as defence attorney Leonard Grisham), while he has played recurring or main characters in _Five Days_ (2007) and _The Passion_ (2008, as Joseph of Arimathea).
In December 2009, he played the leading role of Gilbert in the BBC TV adaptation of Andrea Levy's novel _Small Island_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-17) In March 2010, he played the role of Keme Tobodo in the BBC's drama series _Blood and Oil_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-18) He starred in the HBO original film _Nightingale_ (2014)._[citation needed_]

## Early life and education
He stars in and co-produces the 2023 American western series _Lawmen: Bass Reeves_, based on the life of former slave Bass Reeves who, after the American Civil War, became one of the first Black deputy US Marshals, and the first west of the Mississippi River.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-20)
He appeared as Olaudah Equiano in _Grace Unshackled – The Olaudah Equiano Story_, a radio play adapting Equiano's autobiography, _The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano_. This was first broadcast on BBC 7 on 8 April 2007, with his wife Jessica Oyelowo as Mrs. Equiano.
In 2007, Oyelowo was the reader for John le Carré's _The Mission Song_. _AudioFile_ magazine stated: "Think of David Oyelowo as a single musician playing all the instruments in a symphony. That is essentially what he manages in this inspired performance of John le Carré's suspense novel.... Can it really have been only one man in the narrator's recording booth? This virtuoso performance makes that seem impossible."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-21) In 2015, he was selected to portray James Bond in an audiobook version of _Trigger Mortis_, written by Anthony Horowitz.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-bond-22)

texts.3:
## Early life and education
Oyelowo is an _omoba_ (or prince) of the Yoruba people in the Nigerian chieftaincy system, his grandfather having been king of "a part of Oyo State called Awe". He has commented of his background: "It sounds way more impressive than it actually is. There are so many royal families in Africa",[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-ind1-8) "royal families are a dime a dozen in Nigeria";[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-:1-2) "what we think of as royalty in the UK is very different to royalty in Nigeria: if you were to throw a stone there, you would hit about 30 princes. So, it's a bit more like being the Prince of Islington: it was useful for getting dates but probably not much else."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-11)
Oyelowo attended a "military-style" boarding-school named Lagos State Model College Meiran (now Lagos State Model Junior College Meiran.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-ind1-8) His family returned to London when Oyelowo was 14,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-12) settling in Islington.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-ind1-8)
While enrolled in theatre studies at City and Islington College, his teacher suggested that he become an actor. Oyelowo enrolled for a year in an acting foundation course, at the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art (LAMDA).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-ind1-8) He finished his three-year training in 1998.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-13)
He also spent time with the National Youth Theatre.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-14)
texts.4:
## Early life and education
He began his stage career in 1999 when he was offered a season with the Royal Shakespeare Company playing roles in Ben Jonson's _Volpone_, as the title character in _Oroonoko_ (which he also performed in the BBC radio adaptation) and Shakespeare's_Antony and Cleopatra_ (1999) alongside Guy Henry, Frances de la Tour and Alan Bates. However, he is best known for his next stage performance as King Henry VI[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-big-10) in the Royal Shakespeare Company's 2001 productions of Shakespeare's trilogy of plays about the king as a part of its season _This England: The Histories_. In a major landmark for colour-blind casting, Oyelowo was the first black actor to play an English king in a major production of Shakespeare, and although this casting choice was initially criticised by some in the media, Oyelowo's performance was critically acclaimed and later won the 2001 Ian Charleson Award for best performance by an actor under 30 in a classical play.
In 2005, he appeared in a production of _Prometheus Bound_, which was revived in New York City in 2007. In 2006, he made his directorial debut on a production of _The White Devil_, produced by Inservice, his theatre company in Brighton which is co-run with fellow Brighton-based actors Priyanga Burford, Israel Aduramo, Penelope Cobbuld, and his wife, Jessica.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-15) He played the title role in _Othello_ in 2016 at the New York Theatre Workshop with Daniel Craig as Iago, directed by Sam Gold.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-16) In 2024, he starred in the Royal National Theatre production of Coriolanus.
texts.5:
## Early life and education
Oyelowo is best known for playing MI5 officer Danny Hunter in the British drama series _Spooks_ (known in North America as _MI-5_) from 2002 to 2004. He had before that appeared in _Tomorrow La Scala_ (2002), _Maisie Raine_ (1998) and _Brothers and Sisters_ (1998). Soon after the end of his time on _Spooks_ Oyelowo also appeared in the two Christmas specials of _As Time Goes By_ (2005). In 2006, he appeared in the television film _Born Equal_ alongside Nikki Amuka-Bird as a couple fleeing persecution in Nigeria – they also both appeared in _Shoot the Messenger_ (2006) and in _[The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_No.\_1\_Ladies'\_Detective\_Agency\_(TV\_series) "The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency (TV series)")_ (2008) as a husband and wife. Other cameos have included _Mayo_ (guest-starring on 30 April 2006) and the television film _Sweet Nothing in My Ear_ (2008, as defence attorney Leonard Grisham), while he has played recurring or main characters in _Five Days_ (2007) and _The Passion_ (2008, as Joseph of Arimathea).
In December 2009, he played the leading role of Gilbert in the BBC TV adaptation of Andrea Levy's novel _Small Island_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-17) In March 2010, he played the role of Keme Tobodo in the BBC's drama series _Blood and Oil_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-18) He starred in the HBO original film _Nightingale_ (2014)._[citation needed_]
texts.6:
## Early life and education
He stars in and co-produces the 2023 American western series _Lawmen: Bass Reeves_, based on the life of former slave Bass Reeves who, after the American Civil War, became one of the first Black deputy US Marshals, and the first west of the Mississippi River.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-20)
He appeared as Olaudah Equiano in _Grace Unshackled – The Olaudah Equiano Story_, a radio play adapting Equiano's autobiography, _The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano_. This was first broadcast on BBC 7 on 8 April 2007, with his wife Jessica Oyelowo as Mrs. Equiano.
In 2007, Oyelowo was the reader for John le Carré's _The Mission Song_. _AudioFile_ magazine stated: "Think of David Oyelowo as a single musician playing all the instruments in a symphony. That is essentially what he manages in this inspired performance of John le Carré's suspense novel.... Can it really have been only one man in the narrator's recording booth? This virtuoso performance makes that seem impossible."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-21) In 2015, he was selected to portray James Bond in an audiobook version of _Trigger Mortis_, written by Anthony Horowitz.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-bond-22)

## Early life and education
Oyelowo is an _omoba_ (or prince) of the Yoruba people in the Nigerian chieftaincy system, his grandfather having been king of "a part of Oyo State called Awe". He has commented of his background: "It sounds way more impressive than it actually is. There are so many royal families in Africa",[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-ind1-8) "royal families are a dime a dozen in Nigeria";[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-:1-2) "what we think of as royalty in the UK is very different to royalty in Nigeria: if you were to throw a stone there, you would hit about 30 princes. So, it's a bit more like being the Prince of Islington: it was useful for getting dates but probably not much else."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-11)
Oyelowo attended a "military-style" boarding-school named Lagos State Model College Meiran (now Lagos State Model Junior College Meiran.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-ind1-8) His family returned to London when Oyelowo was 14,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-12) settling in Islington.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-ind1-8)
While enrolled in theatre studies at City and Islington College, his teacher suggested that he become an actor. Oyelowo enrolled for a year in an acting foundation course, at the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art (LAMDA).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-ind1-8) He finished his three-year training in 1998.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-13)
He also spent time with the National Youth Theatre.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-14)

## Early life and education
He began his stage career in 1999 when he was offered a season with the Royal Shakespeare Company playing roles in Ben Jonson's _Volpone_, as the title character in _Oroonoko_ (which he also performed in the BBC radio adaptation) and Shakespeare's_Antony and Cleopatra_ (1999) alongside Guy Henry, Frances de la Tour and Alan Bates. However, he is best known for his next stage performance as King Henry VI[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-big-10) in the Royal Shakespeare Company's 2001 productions of Shakespeare's trilogy of plays about the king as a part of its season _This England: The Histories_. In a major landmark for colour-blind casting, Oyelowo was the first black actor to play an English king in a major production of Shakespeare, and although this casting choice was initially criticised by some in the media, Oyelowo's performance was critically acclaimed and later won the 2001 Ian Charleson Award for best performance by an actor under 30 in a classical play.
In 2005, he appeared in a production of _Prometheus Bound_, which was revived in New York City in 2007. In 2006, he made his directorial debut on a production of _The White Devil_, produced by Inservice, his theatre company in Brighton which is co-run with fellow Brighton-based actors Priyanga Burford, Israel Aduramo, Penelope Cobbuld, and his wife, Jessica.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-15) He played the title role in _Othello_ in 2016 at the New York Theatre Workshop with Daniel Craig as Iago, directed by Sam Gold.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-16) In 2024, he starred in the Royal National Theatre production of Coriolanus.

## Early life and education
Oyelowo is best known for playing MI5 officer Danny Hunter in the British drama series _Spooks_ (known in North America as _MI-5_) from 2002 to 2004. He had before that appeared in _Tomorrow La Scala_ (2002), _Maisie Raine_ (1998) and _Brothers and Sisters_ (1998). Soon after the end of his time on _Spooks_ Oyelowo also appeared in the two Christmas specials of _As Time Goes By_ (2005). In 2006, he appeared in the television film _Born Equal_ alongside Nikki Amuka-Bird as a couple fleeing persecution in Nigeria – they also both appeared in _Shoot the Messenger_ (2006) and in _[The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_No.\_1\_Ladies'\_Detective\_Agency\_(TV\_series) "The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency (TV series)")_ (2008) as a husband and wife. Other cameos have included _Mayo_ (guest-starring on 30 April 2006) and the television film _Sweet Nothing in My Ear_ (2008, as defence attorney Leonard Grisham), while he has played recurring or main characters in _Five Days_ (2007) and _The Passion_ (2008, as Joseph of Arimathea).
In December 2009, he played the leading role of Gilbert in the BBC TV adaptation of Andrea Levy's novel _Small Island_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-17) In March 2010, he played the role of Keme Tobodo in the BBC's drama series _Blood and Oil_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-18) He starred in the HBO original film _Nightingale_ (2014)._[citation needed_]

## Early life and education
He stars in and co-produces the 2023 American western series _Lawmen: Bass Reeves_, based on the life of former slave Bass Reeves who, after the American Civil War, became one of the first Black deputy US Marshals, and the first west of the Mississippi River.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-20)
He appeared as Olaudah Equiano in _Grace Unshackled – The Olaudah Equiano Story_, a radio play adapting Equiano's autobiography, _The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano_. This was first broadcast on BBC 7 on 8 April 2007, with his wife Jessica Oyelowo as Mrs. Equiano.
In 2007, Oyelowo was the reader for John le Carré's _The Mission Song_. _AudioFile_ magazine stated: "Think of David Oyelowo as a single musician playing all the instruments in a symphony. That is essentially what he manages in this inspired performance of John le Carré's suspense novel.... Can it really have been only one man in the narrator's recording booth? This virtuoso performance makes that seem impossible."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-21) In 2015, he was selected to portray James Bond in an audiobook version of _Trigger Mortis_, written by Anthony Horowitz.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo#cite_note-bond-22)

**Kiernan Brennan Shipka** (born November 10, 1999)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-chicago_tribune-2) is an American actress. She is best known for her roles as Sally Draper in the AMC drama series _Mad Men_ (2007–2015), and Sabrina Spellman in the Netflix fantasy series _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ (2018–2020) and the sixth season of The CW series _Riverdale_ (2021–2022).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-deadline-3)
In addition to supporting roles in films such as _Longlegs_, _Twisters_, and _The Last Showgirl_ (all in 2024), Shipka has also had starring roles in _[The Blackcoat's Daughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blackcoat's\_Daughter "The Blackcoat's Daughter")_ (2015), _Totally Killer_ (2023), and _Sweethearts_ (2024), among others.

Kiernan Brennan Shipka was born on November 10, 1999, in Chicago, Illinois, to John Young Shipka, a real-estate developer, and Erin Ann Brennan.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-MadTween-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-6) She is of mostly Irish and Slovak descent.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-7) She also has notable German, English, Scottish, and Italian heritage. Shipka started taking ballroom dancing classes at the age of five and was still attending classes as of March 2012.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-8) When she was six, her family relocated to Los Angeles to help with her acting career.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)

### 2000–2017: Beginnings and _Mad Men_
[edit]
Shipka at the 2010 Screen Actors Guild Awards
In April 2000, Shipka made her television debut at five months of age on the hospital drama _ER_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-dazeddigital-9) She started commercial-print modeling when she was a baby.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-MadTween-4) After undertaking small television roles, her first major role was as Sally Draper, the daughter of main character Don Draper, on the 2007–2015 TV series _Mad Men_. She won the role after two auditions.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-NYT032615-10) She was a recurring guest star for the show's first three seasons, then became a series regular in season four.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)
As part of _Mad Men_'s ensemble cast, she won the Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series in 2008 and 2009.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-11) Shipka received praise for her performance on _Mad Men_. In 2010, _Austin American-Statesman_ critic Dale Roe named her as his dream nominee for the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series, writing, "This 10-year-old actress was so affecting as troubled Sally Draper last season that it seems odd that she's only just been upgraded to series regular. If Shipka's upcoming _Mad Men_ work—struggling with the broken marriage of her parents and entering preteendom in the tumultuous 1960s—remains as amazing as it was in season three, this is a ballot wish that could come true next year."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-roe-12)

### 2000–2017: Beginnings and _Mad Men_
Beginning in 2012, Shipka voiced Jinora in the Nickelodeon animated series _The Legend of Korra_, the sequel to _Avatar: The Last Airbender_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-castinitial-13) In 2014, Shipka was named one of "The 25 Most Influential Teens of 2014" by _Time_ magazine.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-14) That same year, IndieWire included her in their list of "20 Actors To Watch That Are Under 20".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-15) She starred in the 2014 Lifetime movie _Flowers in the Attic_, based on the 1979 novel of the same name by V. C. Andrews.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-16) The following year she co-starred with Emma Roberts in the Osgood Perkins horror film _[The Blackcoat's Daughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blackcoat's\_Daughter "The Blackcoat's Daughter")_, and with Timothée Chalamet in the fantasy thriller _One & Two_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-18) Additionally, she voiced the title character in the English dub of Studio Ghibli's _When Marnie Was There_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-19) In 2017, Shipka portrayed B.D. Hyman, daughter of Bette Davis, in the FX television series _Feud: Bette and Joan_.

### 2018–2021: _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_
[edit]
Shipka in 2018.
In January 2018, Shipka was announced to be starring as Sabrina Spellman in Netflix's _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ series based on the comic series of the same name.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-deadline-3) The first part was released by Netflix on October 26, 2018,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-20) and an episode that December. The show ran for three more parts, concluding on December 31, 2020, with a total of 36 episodes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-21) Shipka reprised the role in two episodes of _Riverdale_, "Chapter Ninety-Nine: The Witching Hour(s)" and "Chapter One Hundred and Fourteen: The Witches of Riverdale", which aired on December 7, 2021, and July 10, 2022, respectively.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-23)

### 2018–2021: _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_
Shipka played a deaf teenager opposite Stanley Tucci in John R. Leonetti's horror film_The Silence_, based on the 2015 novel of the same name by Tim Lebbon.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-24) Netflix released the film on April 10, 2019.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-25) Shipka learned American Sign Language for the role and Leonetti praised her performance, saying: "She's acting alongside Stanley Tucci, and believe me, she's more than holding her own. It's been spellbinding watching her."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-26) That same year, Shipka co-starred in the Christmasromantic comedy film _Let It Snow_, based on the novel _Let It Snow: Three Holiday Romances_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-27)

### 2022–present: Further work
[edit]
In 2022, Shipka starred alongside Diane Kruger in the psychological drama series _Swimming with Sharks_, inspired by the 1994 film of the same name.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-28) She also played Bea Johnson, the daughter of two intellectually disabled parents, in the drama _Wildflower_.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-30) The following year she appeared in the HBO political drama limited series _White House Plumbers_, portraying Kevan Hunt, daughter of E. Howard Hunt.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-31) In October 2023, Shipka starred alongside actress Olivia Holt in Amazon Prime Video's 1980s horror-comedy _Totally Killer_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Hollywood_Reporter-32)

### 2022–present: Further work
In July 2024, Shipka appeared in the horror thriller _Longlegs_, reuniting her with _The Blackcoat's Daughter_ director Osgood Perkins.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-33) Later that year, she had supporting roles in the films _Twisters_, _The Last Showgirl_ and _Red One_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-36) In addition, she co-starred alongside Nico Hiraga in the Max romantic comedy _Sweethearts_,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-37) and in the thriller film _Stone Cold Fox_, which premiered in November 2025.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-38)
In 2026, she appeared in the fourth season of the HBO/BBC drama _Industry_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Shipka,_Farthing,_Jimoh,_and_James-Kelly-39) She also starred in the comedy film _Idiots_, which premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-41)
She is set to star alongside Cole Sprouse in the romantic comedy _Goodbye Girl_,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-42) as well as _The Nowhere Game_, which will reunite her with Mckenna Grace, who portrayed the younger version of her character in _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-43)

**Kiernan Brennan Shipka** (born November 10, 1999)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-chicago_tribune-2) is an American actress. She is best known for her roles as Sally Draper in the AMC drama series _Mad Men_ (2007–2015), and Sabrina Spellman in the Netflix fantasy series _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ (2018–2020) and the sixth season of The CW series _Riverdale_ (2021–2022).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-deadline-3)
In addition to supporting roles in films such as _Longlegs_, _Twisters_, and _The Last Showgirl_ (all in 2024), Shipka has also had starring roles in _[The Blackcoat's Daughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blackcoat's\_Daughter "The Blackcoat's Daughter")_ (2015), _Totally Killer_ (2023), and _Sweethearts_ (2024), among others.
texts.1: Kiernan Brennan Shipka was born on November 10, 1999, in Chicago, Illinois, to John Young Shipka, a real-estate developer, and Erin Ann Brennan.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-MadTween-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-6) She is of mostly Irish and Slovak descent.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-7) She also has notable German, English, Scottish, and Italian heritage. Shipka started taking ballroom dancing classes at the age of five and was still attending classes as of March 2012.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-8) When she was six, her family relocated to Los Angeles to help with her acting career.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)
texts.2:
### 2000–2017: Beginnings and _Mad Men_
[edit]
Shipka at the 2010 Screen Actors Guild Awards
In April 2000, Shipka made her television debut at five months of age on the hospital drama _ER_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-dazeddigital-9) She started commercial-print modeling when she was a baby.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-MadTween-4) After undertaking small television roles, her first major role was as Sally Draper, the daughter of main character Don Draper, on the 2007–2015 TV series _Mad Men_. She won the role after two auditions.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-NYT032615-10) She was a recurring guest star for the show's first three seasons, then became a series regular in season four.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)
As part of _Mad Men_'s ensemble cast, she won the Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series in 2008 and 2009.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-11) Shipka received praise for her performance on _Mad Men_. In 2010, _Austin American-Statesman_ critic Dale Roe named her as his dream nominee for the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series, writing, "This 10-year-old actress was so affecting as troubled Sally Draper last season that it seems odd that she's only just been upgraded to series regular. If Shipka's upcoming _Mad Men_ work—struggling with the broken marriage of her parents and entering preteendom in the tumultuous 1960s—remains as amazing as it was in season three, this is a ballot wish that could come true next year."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-roe-12)
texts.3:
### 2000–2017: Beginnings and _Mad Men_
Beginning in 2012, Shipka voiced Jinora in the Nickelodeon animated series _The Legend of Korra_, the sequel to _Avatar: The Last Airbender_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-castinitial-13) In 2014, Shipka was named one of "The 25 Most Influential Teens of 2014" by _Time_ magazine.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-14) That same year, IndieWire included her in their list of "20 Actors To Watch That Are Under 20".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-15) She starred in the 2014 Lifetime movie _Flowers in the Attic_, based on the 1979 novel of the same name by V. C. Andrews.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-16) The following year she co-starred with Emma Roberts in the Osgood Perkins horror film _[The Blackcoat's Daughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blackcoat's\_Daughter "The Blackcoat's Daughter")_, and with Timothée Chalamet in the fantasy thriller _One & Two_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-18) Additionally, she voiced the title character in the English dub of Studio Ghibli's _When Marnie Was There_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-19) In 2017, Shipka portrayed B.D. Hyman, daughter of Bette Davis, in the FX television series _Feud: Bette and Joan_.
texts.4:
### 2018–2021: _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_
[edit]
Shipka in 2018.
In January 2018, Shipka was announced to be starring as Sabrina Spellman in Netflix's _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ series based on the comic series of the same name.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-deadline-3) The first part was released by Netflix on October 26, 2018,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-20) and an episode that December. The show ran for three more parts, concluding on December 31, 2020, with a total of 36 episodes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-21) Shipka reprised the role in two episodes of _Riverdale_, "Chapter Ninety-Nine: The Witching Hour(s)" and "Chapter One Hundred and Fourteen: The Witches of Riverdale", which aired on December 7, 2021, and July 10, 2022, respectively.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-23)
texts.5:
### 2018–2021: _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_
Shipka played a deaf teenager opposite Stanley Tucci in John R. Leonetti's horror film_The Silence_, based on the 2015 novel of the same name by Tim Lebbon.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-24) Netflix released the film on April 10, 2019.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-25) Shipka learned American Sign Language for the role and Leonetti praised her performance, saying: "She's acting alongside Stanley Tucci, and believe me, she's more than holding her own. It's been spellbinding watching her."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-26) That same year, Shipka co-starred in the Christmasromantic comedy film _Let It Snow_, based on the novel _Let It Snow: Three Holiday Romances_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-27)
texts.6:
### 2022–present: Further work
[edit]
In 2022, Shipka starred alongside Diane Kruger in the psychological drama series _Swimming with Sharks_, inspired by the 1994 film of the same name.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-28) She also played Bea Johnson, the daughter of two intellectually disabled parents, in the drama _Wildflower_.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-30) The following year she appeared in the HBO political drama limited series _White House Plumbers_, portraying Kevan Hunt, daughter of E. Howard Hunt.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-31) In October 2023, Shipka starred alongside actress Olivia Holt in Amazon Prime Video's 1980s horror-comedy _Totally Killer_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Hollywood_Reporter-32)
texts.7:
### 2022–present: Further work
In July 2024, Shipka appeared in the horror thriller _Longlegs_, reuniting her with _The Blackcoat's Daughter_ director Osgood Perkins.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-33) Later that year, she had supporting roles in the films _Twisters_, _The Last Showgirl_ and _Red One_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-36) In addition, she co-starred alongside Nico Hiraga in the Max romantic comedy _Sweethearts_,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-37) and in the thriller film _Stone Cold Fox_, which premiered in November 2025.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-38)
In 2026, she appeared in the fourth season of the HBO/BBC drama _Industry_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Shipka,_Farthing,_Jimoh,_and_James-Kelly-39) She also starred in the comedy film _Idiots_, which premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-41)
She is set to star alongside Cole Sprouse in the romantic comedy _Goodbye Girl_,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-42) as well as _The Nowhere Game_, which will reunite her with Mckenna Grace, who portrayed the younger version of her character in _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-43)

**Kiernan Brennan Shipka** (born November 10, 1999)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-chicago_tribune-2) is an American actress. She is best known for her roles as Sally Draper in the AMC drama series _Mad Men_ (2007–2015), and Sabrina Spellman in the Netflix fantasy series _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ (2018–2020) and the sixth season of The CW series _Riverdale_ (2021–2022).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-deadline-3)
In addition to supporting roles in films such as _Longlegs_, _Twisters_, and _The Last Showgirl_ (all in 2024), Shipka has also had starring roles in _[The Blackcoat's Daughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blackcoat's\_Daughter "The Blackcoat's Daughter")_ (2015), _Totally Killer_ (2023), and _Sweethearts_ (2024), among others.

Kiernan Brennan Shipka was born on November 10, 1999, in Chicago, Illinois, to John Young Shipka, a real-estate developer, and Erin Ann Brennan.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-MadTween-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-6) She is of mostly Irish and Slovak descent.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-7) She also has notable German, English, Scottish, and Italian heritage. Shipka started taking ballroom dancing classes at the age of five and was still attending classes as of March 2012.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-8) When she was six, her family relocated to Los Angeles to help with her acting career.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)

### 2000–2017: Beginnings and _Mad Men_
[edit]
Shipka at the 2010 Screen Actors Guild Awards
In April 2000, Shipka made her television debut at five months of age on the hospital drama _ER_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-dazeddigital-9) She started commercial-print modeling when she was a baby.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-MadTween-4) After undertaking small television roles, her first major role was as Sally Draper, the daughter of main character Don Draper, on the 2007–2015 TV series _Mad Men_. She won the role after two auditions.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-NYT032615-10) She was a recurring guest star for the show's first three seasons, then became a series regular in season four.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)
As part of _Mad Men_'s ensemble cast, she won the Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series in 2008 and 2009.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-11) Shipka received praise for her performance on _Mad Men_. In 2010, _Austin American-Statesman_ critic Dale Roe named her as his dream nominee for the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series, writing, "This 10-year-old actress was so affecting as troubled Sally Draper last season that it seems odd that she's only just been upgraded to series regular. If Shipka's upcoming _Mad Men_ work—struggling with the broken marriage of her parents and entering preteendom in the tumultuous 1960s—remains as amazing as it was in season three, this is a ballot wish that could come true next year."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-roe-12)

### 2000–2017: Beginnings and _Mad Men_
Beginning in 2012, Shipka voiced Jinora in the Nickelodeon animated series _The Legend of Korra_, the sequel to _Avatar: The Last Airbender_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-castinitial-13) In 2014, Shipka was named one of "The 25 Most Influential Teens of 2014" by _Time_ magazine.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-14) That same year, IndieWire included her in their list of "20 Actors To Watch That Are Under 20".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-15) She starred in the 2014 Lifetime movie _Flowers in the Attic_, based on the 1979 novel of the same name by V. C. Andrews.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-16) The following year she co-starred with Emma Roberts in the Osgood Perkins horror film _[The Blackcoat's Daughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blackcoat's\_Daughter "The Blackcoat's Daughter")_, and with Timothée Chalamet in the fantasy thriller _One & Two_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-18) Additionally, she voiced the title character in the English dub of Studio Ghibli's _When Marnie Was There_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-19) In 2017, Shipka portrayed B.D. Hyman, daughter of Bette Davis, in the FX television series _Feud: Bette and Joan_.

### 2018–2021: _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_
[edit]
Shipka in 2018.
In January 2018, Shipka was announced to be starring as Sabrina Spellman in Netflix's _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ series based on the comic series of the same name.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-deadline-3) The first part was released by Netflix on October 26, 2018,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-20) and an episode that December. The show ran for three more parts, concluding on December 31, 2020, with a total of 36 episodes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-21) Shipka reprised the role in two episodes of _Riverdale_, "Chapter Ninety-Nine: The Witching Hour(s)" and "Chapter One Hundred and Fourteen: The Witches of Riverdale", which aired on December 7, 2021, and July 10, 2022, respectively.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-23)

### 2018–2021: _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_
Shipka played a deaf teenager opposite Stanley Tucci in John R. Leonetti's horror film_The Silence_, based on the 2015 novel of the same name by Tim Lebbon.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-24) Netflix released the film on April 10, 2019.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-25) Shipka learned American Sign Language for the role and Leonetti praised her performance, saying: "She's acting alongside Stanley Tucci, and believe me, she's more than holding her own. It's been spellbinding watching her."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-26) That same year, Shipka co-starred in the Christmasromantic comedy film _Let It Snow_, based on the novel _Let It Snow: Three Holiday Romances_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-27)

### 2022–present: Further work
[edit]
In 2022, Shipka starred alongside Diane Kruger in the psychological drama series _Swimming with Sharks_, inspired by the 1994 film of the same name.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-28) She also played Bea Johnson, the daughter of two intellectually disabled parents, in the drama _Wildflower_.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-30) The following year she appeared in the HBO political drama limited series _White House Plumbers_, portraying Kevan Hunt, daughter of E. Howard Hunt.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-31) In October 2023, Shipka starred alongside actress Olivia Holt in Amazon Prime Video's 1980s horror-comedy _Totally Killer_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Hollywood_Reporter-32)

### 2022–present: Further work
In July 2024, Shipka appeared in the horror thriller _Longlegs_, reuniting her with _The Blackcoat's Daughter_ director Osgood Perkins.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-33) Later that year, she had supporting roles in the films _Twisters_, _The Last Showgirl_ and _Red One_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-36) In addition, she co-starred alongside Nico Hiraga in the Max romantic comedy _Sweethearts_,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-37) and in the thriller film _Stone Cold Fox_, which premiered in November 2025.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-38)
In 2026, she appeared in the fourth season of the HBO/BBC drama _Industry_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Shipka,_Farthing,_Jimoh,_and_James-Kelly-39) She also starred in the comedy film _Idiots_, which premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-41)
She is set to star alongside Cole Sprouse in the romantic comedy _Goodbye Girl_,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-42) as well as _The Nowhere Game_, which will reunite her with Mckenna Grace, who portrayed the younger version of her character in _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-43)

### 2018–2021: _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_
[edit]
Shipka in 2018.
In January 2018, Shipka was announced to be starring as Sabrina Spellman in Netflix's _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ series based on the comic series of the same name.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-deadline-3) The first part was released by Netflix on October 26, 2018,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-20) and an episode that December. The show ran for three more parts, concluding on December 31, 2020, with a total of 36 episodes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-21) Shipka reprised the role in two episodes of _Riverdale_, "Chapter Ninety-Nine: The Witching Hour(s)" and "Chapter One Hundred and Fourteen: The Witches of Riverdale", which aired on December 7, 2021, and July 10, 2022, respectively.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-23)

### 2018–2021: _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_
Shipka played a deaf teenager opposite Stanley Tucci in John R. Leonetti's horror film_The Silence_, based on the 2015 novel of the same name by Tim Lebbon.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-24) Netflix released the film on April 10, 2019.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-25) Shipka learned American Sign Language for the role and Leonetti praised her performance, saying: "She's acting alongside Stanley Tucci, and believe me, she's more than holding her own. It's been spellbinding watching her."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-26) That same year, Shipka co-starred in the Christmasromantic comedy film _Let It Snow_, based on the novel _Let It Snow: Three Holiday Romances_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-27)

### 2022–present: Further work
[edit]
In 2022, Shipka starred alongside Diane Kruger in the psychological drama series _Swimming with Sharks_, inspired by the 1994 film of the same name.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-28) She also played Bea Johnson, the daughter of two intellectually disabled parents, in the drama _Wildflower_.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-30) The following year she appeared in the HBO political drama limited series _White House Plumbers_, portraying Kevan Hunt, daughter of E. Howard Hunt.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-31) In October 2023, Shipka starred alongside actress Olivia Holt in Amazon Prime Video's 1980s horror-comedy _Totally Killer_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Hollywood_Reporter-32)

### 2022–present: Further work
In July 2024, Shipka appeared in the horror thriller _Longlegs_, reuniting her with _The Blackcoat's Daughter_ director Osgood Perkins.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-33) Later that year, she had supporting roles in the films _Twisters_, _The Last Showgirl_ and _Red One_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-36) In addition, she co-starred alongside Nico Hiraga in the Max romantic comedy _Sweethearts_,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-37) and in the thriller film _Stone Cold Fox_, which premiered in November 2025.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-38)
In 2026, she appeared in the fourth season of the HBO/BBC drama _Industry_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Shipka,_Farthing,_Jimoh,_and_James-Kelly-39) She also starred in the comedy film _Idiots_, which premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-41)
She is set to star alongside Cole Sprouse in the romantic comedy _Goodbye Girl_,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-42) as well as _The Nowhere Game_, which will reunite her with Mckenna Grace, who portrayed the younger version of her character in _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-43)

### 2018–2021: _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_
[edit]
Shipka in 2018.
In January 2018, Shipka was announced to be starring as Sabrina Spellman in Netflix's _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ series based on the comic series of the same name.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-deadline-3) The first part was released by Netflix on October 26, 2018,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-20) and an episode that December. The show ran for three more parts, concluding on December 31, 2020, with a total of 36 episodes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-21) Shipka reprised the role in two episodes of _Riverdale_, "Chapter Ninety-Nine: The Witching Hour(s)" and "Chapter One Hundred and Fourteen: The Witches of Riverdale", which aired on December 7, 2021, and July 10, 2022, respectively.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-23)
texts.5:
### 2018–2021: _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_
Shipka played a deaf teenager opposite Stanley Tucci in John R. Leonetti's horror film_The Silence_, based on the 2015 novel of the same name by Tim Lebbon.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-24) Netflix released the film on April 10, 2019.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-25) Shipka learned American Sign Language for the role and Leonetti praised her performance, saying: "She's acting alongside Stanley Tucci, and believe me, she's more than holding her own. It's been spellbinding watching her."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-26) That same year, Shipka co-starred in the Christmasromantic comedy film _Let It Snow_, based on the novel _Let It Snow: Three Holiday Romances_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-27)
texts.6:
### 2022–present: Further work
[edit]
In 2022, Shipka starred alongside Diane Kruger in the psychological drama series _Swimming with Sharks_, inspired by the 1994 film of the same name.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-28) She also played Bea Johnson, the daughter of two intellectually disabled parents, in the drama _Wildflower_.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-30) The following year she appeared in the HBO political drama limited series _White House Plumbers_, portraying Kevan Hunt, daughter of E. Howard Hunt.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-31) In October 2023, Shipka starred alongside actress Olivia Holt in Amazon Prime Video's 1980s horror-comedy _Totally Killer_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Hollywood_Reporter-32)
texts.7:
### 2022–present: Further work
In July 2024, Shipka appeared in the horror thriller _Longlegs_, reuniting her with _The Blackcoat's Daughter_ director Osgood Perkins.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-33) Later that year, she had supporting roles in the films _Twisters_, _The Last Showgirl_ and _Red One_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-36) In addition, she co-starred alongside Nico Hiraga in the Max romantic comedy _Sweethearts_,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-37) and in the thriller film _Stone Cold Fox_, which premiered in November 2025.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-38)
In 2026, she appeared in the fourth season of the HBO/BBC drama _Industry_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Shipka,_Farthing,_Jimoh,_and_James-Kelly-39) She also starred in the comedy film _Idiots_, which premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-41)
She is set to star alongside Cole Sprouse in the romantic comedy _Goodbye Girl_,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-42) as well as _The Nowhere Game_, which will reunite her with Mckenna Grace, who portrayed the younger version of her character in _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-43)

### 2018–2021: _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_
[edit]
Shipka in 2018.
In January 2018, Shipka was announced to be starring as Sabrina Spellman in Netflix's _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ series based on the comic series of the same name.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-deadline-3) The first part was released by Netflix on October 26, 2018,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-20) and an episode that December. The show ran for three more parts, concluding on December 31, 2020, with a total of 36 episodes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-21) Shipka reprised the role in two episodes of _Riverdale_, "Chapter Ninety-Nine: The Witching Hour(s)" and "Chapter One Hundred and Fourteen: The Witches of Riverdale", which aired on December 7, 2021, and July 10, 2022, respectively.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-23)

### 2018–2021: _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_
Shipka played a deaf teenager opposite Stanley Tucci in John R. Leonetti's horror film_The Silence_, based on the 2015 novel of the same name by Tim Lebbon.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-24) Netflix released the film on April 10, 2019.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-25) Shipka learned American Sign Language for the role and Leonetti praised her performance, saying: "She's acting alongside Stanley Tucci, and believe me, she's more than holding her own. It's been spellbinding watching her."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-26) That same year, Shipka co-starred in the Christmasromantic comedy film _Let It Snow_, based on the novel _Let It Snow: Three Holiday Romances_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-27)

### 2022–present: Further work
[edit]
In 2022, Shipka starred alongside Diane Kruger in the psychological drama series _Swimming with Sharks_, inspired by the 1994 film of the same name.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-28) She also played Bea Johnson, the daughter of two intellectually disabled parents, in the drama _Wildflower_.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-30) The following year she appeared in the HBO political drama limited series _White House Plumbers_, portraying Kevan Hunt, daughter of E. Howard Hunt.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-31) In October 2023, Shipka starred alongside actress Olivia Holt in Amazon Prime Video's 1980s horror-comedy _Totally Killer_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Hollywood_Reporter-32)

### 2022–present: Further work
In July 2024, Shipka appeared in the horror thriller _Longlegs_, reuniting her with _The Blackcoat's Daughter_ director Osgood Perkins.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-33) Later that year, she had supporting roles in the films _Twisters_, _The Last Showgirl_ and _Red One_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-36) In addition, she co-starred alongside Nico Hiraga in the Max romantic comedy _Sweethearts_,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-37) and in the thriller film _Stone Cold Fox_, which premiered in November 2025.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-38)
In 2026, she appeared in the fourth season of the HBO/BBC drama _Industry_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Shipka,_Farthing,_Jimoh,_and_James-Kelly-39) She also starred in the comedy film _Idiots_, which premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-41)
She is set to star alongside Cole Sprouse in the romantic comedy _Goodbye Girl_,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-42) as well as _The Nowhere Game_, which will reunite her with Mckenna Grace, who portrayed the younger version of her character in _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-43)

Title: Urmila Matondkar
Chunks: 21,22,23,24,25,26,27,32,33,34,35
In 2007, Matondkar appeared in an item song in Ram Gopal Varma's _Aag_[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-88) and was later seen in a cameo in the ensemble song "Deewangi Deewangi", in Farah Khan's _Om Shanti Om_.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-89) In the same year, she was seen in the action-thriller _Speed_ as part of an ensemble cast.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Speed_Movie_Review-90) Noting her reduced acting appearances during this phase, Taran Adarsh wrote in his review, "Urmila handles her part with dexterity and adds freshness to the goings-on since she has cut down on her acting assignments".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Speed_Movie_Review-90)
The next year, Matondkar appeared alongside Himesh Reshammiya in the thriller _Karzzzz_ (2008), a remake of the 1980 film _Karz_.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_in_Karzzzz_and_EMI-91) Her performance as Kamini (originally played by Simi Garewal) received praise, although the film was a critical and commercial failure.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-92) She also re-united with Sanjay Dutt for the social-comedy _EMI - Liya Hai Toh Chukana Padega!_ in the same year.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_in_Karzzzz_and_EMI-91)_EMI_ remains Matondkar's last leading role in Bollywood to date, although she continued to appear occasionally in films and television in the following years.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-93)

After a four-year absence from major film roles, Matondkar returned to films by voicing the character of Begum in the Hindi version of the animated musical comedy _Delhi Safari_, released in 2012.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-urmila-matondkar-comes-back-94) The same year, she made a special appearance in an item song in the Marathi film _Hridayanath_, starring Jackie Shroff. In 2013, she was seen in a cameo role in the adventure-comedy _Life Mein Hungama Hai_, which released after a delay of several years and went unnoticed.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-95)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_on_Dance_India_Dance_Super_Moms-8)
In 2014, Matondkar appeared in her first full-fledged role in Marathi cinema in the adventure-drama _Ajoba_.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-96) In the film, she portrayed Purva Rao, a wildlife activist in search of leopards. Praising her performance, _Daily News and Analysis_ wrote, "..this one's another jewel in her crown. She portrays Purva with a mild aggressive and rebellious streak. But all of these are an undercurrent to Purva's actions."[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-97)
Matondkar at a film screening in 2025.

In 2018, Matondkar ventured into film-production with the Marathi film _Madhuri_, as a co-producer along with her husband Mohsin Akhtar, under the banner _Mumbapuri Productions_.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_Matondkar_turns_producer-98) In the same year, she made a very brief return to Bollywood with a special appearance in the dark comedy _Blackmail_, in the song "Bewafa Beauty".[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-99)
In 2022, Matondkar was announced to star with Shreyas Talpade in a Marathi film titled _Tee Mee Navhech_. However, no significant updates on the project have been announced since.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-100)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-101) Later that year, she was announced to make her OTT debut with the action-thriller web series _Tiwari_, in which she plays the title role in a story centred on a mother and daughter.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-102) The series has subsequently faced post-production delays, and is unreleased as of 2026.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-103)
Matondkar has also been roped in for another upcoming IIT-based series produced by TVF, slated for release in mid-2027.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-104)

Alongside her film career, Matondkar has appeared as a celebrity guest on several reality television programmes, like _Movers & Shakers_, _Boogie Woogie_[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-105) and _The Manish Malhotra Show_. She also presented an episode of Sahara TV's _Dil Ki Baatein_ series in 2003, which featured Bollywood celebrities presenting vignettes from their personal lives.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-106)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-107).

In 2006, Matondkar was announced as a judge on Sahara One's reality show _Superstars_ alongside choreographer Shiamak Davar,[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-108)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-109)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-110) although the show was apparently shelved. However, a year later, she and Davar joined veteran actor Jeetendra as judges for the second season of Sony's dance reality show _Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa_.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Matondkar_on_Jhalak_Dikhla_Ja-111) Describing her experience of judging the show, Matondkar said, "I'm ecstatic about being able to be part of this show. I was facing the participants and audience for the first time. There were no written lines, no cues, no second chances. Either it worked or it didn't work for you. It was a concept that I liked."[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Matondkar_on_Jhalak_Dikhla_Ja-111) The next year, she hosted the singing reality show _Waar Parriwar_ on the same channel.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-112) She mentioned in an interview that she agreed to host the show because she felt comfortable with its family-oriented format, and also emphasized her preference for authenticity over scripted drama in reality TV.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-113)
Matondkar on the sets of _Chak Dhoom Dhoom season 2_ in 2011.

In 2011, she was roped in for the second season of Colors' dance reality show _Chak Dhoom Dhoom_.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-urmila-matondkar-comes-back-94) She replaced Mallika Sherawat, and joined Javed Jaffrey and Terence Lewis in the judging panel.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-114)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-115) Matondkar subsequently ventured into Marathi television, with Zee Marathi's dance reality show _Marathi Paaul Padte Pudhe_ (2011–2012), where she served as a judge in its second season.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-116) She then featured as the 'Grand Master' judge in _Dance Maharashtra Dance_ (2012–2013), on the same channel.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-117)
After ten years, Matondkar returned to Hindi television with the third season of _DID Super Moms_ (2022), on Zee TV.

She featured as a co-judge alongside [Remo D'Souza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remo_D'Souza "Remo D'Souza") and Bhagyashree.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_Matondkar_defends_projection_of_contestants'_sob_stories-118)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_on_Dance_India_Dance_Super_Moms-8) In an interview for the show, she supported the inclusion of personal backstories of the contestants on reality television, stating that it was important for audiences to understand their journeys and struggles.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_Matondkar_defends_projection_of_contestants'_sob_stories-118) Matondkar continues to make occasional appearances as a guest in shows like _Indian Idol_,[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-119)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-120)_Sa Re Ga Ma Pa_,[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-121)_Dance Deewane_,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-122)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-123)_Zee Comedy Show_,[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-124)_Khupte Tithe Gupte_[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-125) and _[India's Best Dancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India's\_Best\_Dancer\_(Hindi\_TV\_series) "India's Best Dancer (Hindi TV series)")_.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-126)

In 2004, Matondkar featured in the music video of the song "Deewanay", by the Pakistani pop-rock band Fuzön, directed by Prahlad Kakkar and Saqib Malik.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-164)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-165) The collaboration aimed at promoting India–Pakistan peace and cultural exchange, drawing major media attention when she visited Lahore to shoot the video.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-166) In 2007, Matondkar marked a rare venture into singing by lending her vocals to the song "Mehbooba Dilruba", for Asha Bhonsle's music album _Asha & Friends Vol. 1_, and also appeared in the accompanying video of the song with Bhonsle.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-167)[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-168)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-169)
[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shabana,_Urmila_and_Dia_supporting_Anna_Hazare's_movement.jpg)
Matondkar in a rally for Anna Hazare's movement, alongside Shabana Azmi and Dia Mirza, in 2011.
Prior to entering active politics, Matondkar was associated with various charitable initiatives and has particularly supported causes related to the empowerment of women in India. She was among several film personalities who rallied in support of Anna Hazare's anti-corruption movement in 2011 in Mumbai.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-170)

Matondkar officially joined the Indian National Congress on 27 March 2019.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-171) She stated in an interview that she had been approached for political roles earlier in her career too, but had chosen to decline them before eventually entering politics due to socio-political concerns.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-172) She contested from Mumbai North constituency in the 2019 Lok Sabha Election.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-173) She lost out to Gopal Shetty of the Bhartiya Janta Party, who retained the seat by a massive margin of over 4 lakhs votes.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-174) She resigned from the party on 10 September 2019 by submitting her writing to Sonia Gandhi (then interim chief of the Congress), and cited "petty in-house politics" as a reason behind her resignation.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-175)
On 1 December 2020, Matondkar joined the Shiv Sena in presence of party president Uddhav Thackeray.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Quint2020-176)[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-177) Shiv Sena hoped to add a nationally recognised face and voice, well conversant in Marathi, Hindi as well as English, to represent the party.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Quint2020-176) In 2022, she participated in _Bharat Jodo Yatra_, joining Rahul Gandhi during the march, despite having earlier left the Congress.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-178)

Matondkar has been described by critics as one of the most talented actresses of Indian cinema and has also been praised for her dancing skills.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-179)[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila's_best_dance_sequences-180)_The Tribune_ described her as a versatile actress and a "glam doll" who successfully transitioned from child artist roles to a leading performer.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Glamdoll-2001-181) Following the success of _Rangeela_ (1995), media coverage frequently described Matondkar as a "sex symbol" of contemporary Hindi cinema, a label that she acknowledged as being shaped largely by publicity and promotional framing, which contributed to her being typecast.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Srinivasan,_V_S-5) She was included in _The Tribune_'s list of Bollywood's top five actresses of 1998.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Top-5-actresses-1998-182)
Matondkar in 2010

By the early 2000s, publications such as _Rediff_ noted that she had moved beyond the early "glamour" label, establishing herself through varied and often unconventional roles in films such as _Kaun?_, _Bhoot_, and _Pinjar_. Because she could go from being the ultimate glamour girl to being completely de-glammed and terrified in a dark apartment, the film press in that era often described her as "The Goddess" — someone who could hold audience with just her eyes, whether she was dancing or in complete silence. In a 2003 feature interview in _The Tribune_, Matondkar was described as an established actress whose career included both commercial films and roles across varied genres.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-TribuneSpectrum-183) She featured in _Rediff'_ s "Top Bollywood Actresses" listing in the same year.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-184)
> "I have always tried to make life interesting for myself by doing different roles that connect mainstream cinema with its offbeat counterpart. I guess I have been daring and lucky with my roles. I want to do every kind of role with a reasonable amount of panache. I want to be a fair combination of style and substance"
—Matondkar on her approach to acting, during an interview in 2002.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Sukanya_Verma-185)
