texts.21:
In 2007, Matondkar appeared in an item song in Ram Gopal Varma's _Aag_[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-88) and was later seen in a cameo in the ensemble song "Deewangi Deewangi", in Farah Khan's _Om Shanti Om_.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-89) In the same year, she was seen in the action-thriller _Speed_ as part of an ensemble cast.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Speed_Movie_Review-90) Noting her reduced acting appearances during this phase, Taran Adarsh wrote in his review, "Urmila handles her part with dexterity and adds freshness to the goings-on since she has cut down on her acting assignments".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Speed_Movie_Review-90)
The next year, Matondkar appeared alongside Himesh Reshammiya in the thriller _Karzzzz_ (2008), a remake of the 1980 film _Karz_.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_in_Karzzzz_and_EMI-91) Her performance as Kamini (originally played by Simi Garewal) received praise, although the film was a critical and commercial failure.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-92) She also re-united with Sanjay Dutt for the social-comedy _EMI - Liya Hai Toh Chukana Padega!_ in the same year.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_in_Karzzzz_and_EMI-91)_EMI_ remains Matondkar's last leading role in Bollywood to date, although she continued to appear occasionally in films and television in the following years.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-93)
texts.22:
After a four-year absence from major film roles, Matondkar returned to films by voicing the character of Begum in the Hindi version of the animated musical comedy _Delhi Safari_, released in 2012.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-urmila-matondkar-comes-back-94) The same year, she made a special appearance in an item song in the Marathi film _Hridayanath_, starring Jackie Shroff. In 2013, she was seen in a cameo role in the adventure-comedy _Life Mein Hungama Hai_, which released after a delay of several years and went unnoticed.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-95)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_on_Dance_India_Dance_Super_Moms-8)
In 2014, Matondkar appeared in her first full-fledged role in Marathi cinema in the adventure-drama _Ajoba_.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-96) In the film, she portrayed Purva Rao, a wildlife activist in search of leopards. Praising her performance, _Daily News and Analysis_ wrote, "..this one's another jewel in her crown. She portrays Purva with a mild aggressive and rebellious streak. But all of these are an undercurrent to Purva's actions."[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-97)
Matondkar at a film screening in 2025.
texts.23:
In 2018, Matondkar ventured into film-production with the Marathi film _Madhuri_, as a co-producer along with her husband Mohsin Akhtar, under the banner _Mumbapuri Productions_.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_Matondkar_turns_producer-98) In the same year, she made a very brief return to Bollywood with a special appearance in the dark comedy _Blackmail_, in the song "Bewafa Beauty".[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-99)
In 2022, Matondkar was announced to star with Shreyas Talpade in a Marathi film titled _Tee Mee Navhech_. However, no significant updates on the project have been announced since.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-100)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-101) Later that year, she was announced to make her OTT debut with the action-thriller web series _Tiwari_, in which she plays the title role in a story centred on a mother and daughter.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-102) The series has subsequently faced post-production delays, and is unreleased as of 2026.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-103)
Matondkar has also been roped in for another upcoming IIT-based series produced by TVF, slated for release in mid-2027.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-104)
texts.24: Alongside her film career, Matondkar has appeared as a celebrity guest on several reality television programmes, like _Movers & Shakers_, _Boogie Woogie_[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-105) and _The Manish Malhotra Show_. She also presented an episode of Sahara TV's _Dil Ki Baatein_ series in 2003, which featured Bollywood celebrities presenting vignettes from their personal lives.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-106)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-107).
texts.25:
In 2006, Matondkar was announced as a judge on Sahara One's reality show _Superstars_ alongside choreographer Shiamak Davar,[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-108)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-109)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-110) although the show was apparently shelved. However, a year later, she and Davar joined veteran actor Jeetendra as judges for the second season of Sony's dance reality show _Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa_.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Matondkar_on_Jhalak_Dikhla_Ja-111) Describing her experience of judging the show, Matondkar said, "I'm ecstatic about being able to be part of this show. I was facing the participants and audience for the first time. There were no written lines, no cues, no second chances. Either it worked or it didn't work for you. It was a concept that I liked."[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Matondkar_on_Jhalak_Dikhla_Ja-111) The next year, she hosted the singing reality show _Waar Parriwar_ on the same channel.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-112) She mentioned in an interview that she agreed to host the show because she felt comfortable with its family-oriented format, and also emphasized her preference for authenticity over scripted drama in reality TV.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-113)
Matondkar on the sets of _Chak Dhoom Dhoom season 2_ in 2011.
texts.26:
In 2011, she was roped in for the second season of Colors' dance reality show _Chak Dhoom Dhoom_.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-urmila-matondkar-comes-back-94) She replaced Mallika Sherawat, and joined Javed Jaffrey and Terence Lewis in the judging panel.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-114)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-115) Matondkar subsequently ventured into Marathi television, with Zee Marathi's dance reality show _Marathi Paaul Padte Pudhe_ (2011–2012), where she served as a judge in its second season.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-116) She then featured as the 'Grand Master' judge in _Dance Maharashtra Dance_ (2012–2013), on the same channel.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-117)
After ten years, Matondkar returned to Hindi television with the third season of _DID Super Moms_ (2022), on Zee TV.
texts.27: She featured as a co-judge alongside [Remo D'Souza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remo_D'Souza "Remo D'Souza") and Bhagyashree.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_Matondkar_defends_projection_of_contestants'_sob_stories-118)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_on_Dance_India_Dance_Super_Moms-8) In an interview for the show, she supported the inclusion of personal backstories of the contestants on reality television, stating that it was important for audiences to understand their journeys and struggles.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_Matondkar_defends_projection_of_contestants'_sob_stories-118) Matondkar continues to make occasional appearances as a guest in shows like _Indian Idol_,[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-119)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-120)_Sa Re Ga Ma Pa_,[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-121)_Dance Deewane_,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-122)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-123)_Zee Comedy Show_,[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-124)_Khupte Tithe Gupte_[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-125) and _[India's Best Dancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India's\_Best\_Dancer\_(Hindi\_TV\_series) "India's Best Dancer (Hindi TV series)")_.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-126)
texts.32:
In 2004, Matondkar featured in the music video of the song "Deewanay", by the Pakistani pop-rock band Fuzön, directed by Prahlad Kakkar and Saqib Malik.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-164)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-165) The collaboration aimed at promoting India–Pakistan peace and cultural exchange, drawing major media attention when she visited Lahore to shoot the video.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-166) In 2007, Matondkar marked a rare venture into singing by lending her vocals to the song "Mehbooba Dilruba", for Asha Bhonsle's music album _Asha & Friends Vol. 1_, and also appeared in the accompanying video of the song with Bhonsle.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-167)[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-168)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-169)
[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shabana,_Urmila_and_Dia_supporting_Anna_Hazare's_movement.jpg)
Matondkar in a rally for Anna Hazare's movement, alongside Shabana Azmi and Dia Mirza, in 2011.
Prior to entering active politics, Matondkar was associated with various charitable initiatives and has particularly supported causes related to the empowerment of women in India. She was among several film personalities who rallied in support of Anna Hazare's anti-corruption movement in 2011 in Mumbai.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-170)
texts.33:
Matondkar officially joined the Indian National Congress on 27 March 2019.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-171) She stated in an interview that she had been approached for political roles earlier in her career too, but had chosen to decline them before eventually entering politics due to socio-political concerns.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-172) She contested from Mumbai North constituency in the 2019 Lok Sabha Election.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-173) She lost out to Gopal Shetty of the Bhartiya Janta Party, who retained the seat by a massive margin of over 4 lakhs votes.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-174) She resigned from the party on 10 September 2019 by submitting her writing to Sonia Gandhi (then interim chief of the Congress), and cited "petty in-house politics" as a reason behind her resignation.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-175)
On 1 December 2020, Matondkar joined the Shiv Sena in presence of party president Uddhav Thackeray.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Quint2020-176)[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-177) Shiv Sena hoped to add a nationally recognised face and voice, well conversant in Marathi, Hindi as well as English, to represent the party.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Quint2020-176) In 2022, she participated in _Bharat Jodo Yatra_, joining Rahul Gandhi during the march, despite having earlier left the Congress.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-178)
texts.34:
Matondkar has been described by critics as one of the most talented actresses of Indian cinema and has also been praised for her dancing skills.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-179)[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila's_best_dance_sequences-180)_The Tribune_ described her as a versatile actress and a "glam doll" who successfully transitioned from child artist roles to a leading performer.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Glamdoll-2001-181) Following the success of _Rangeela_ (1995), media coverage frequently described Matondkar as a "sex symbol" of contemporary Hindi cinema, a label that she acknowledged as being shaped largely by publicity and promotional framing, which contributed to her being typecast.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Srinivasan,_V_S-5) She was included in _The Tribune_'s list of Bollywood's top five actresses of 1998.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Top-5-actresses-1998-182)
Matondkar in 2010
texts.35:
By the early 2000s, publications such as _Rediff_ noted that she had moved beyond the early "glamour" label, establishing herself through varied and often unconventional roles in films such as _Kaun?_, _Bhoot_, and _Pinjar_. Because she could go from being the ultimate glamour girl to being completely de-glammed and terrified in a dark apartment, the film press in that era often described her as "The Goddess" — someone who could hold audience with just her eyes, whether she was dancing or in complete silence. In a 2003 feature interview in _The Tribune_, Matondkar was described as an established actress whose career included both commercial films and roles across varied genres.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-TribuneSpectrum-183) She featured in _Rediff'_ s "Top Bollywood Actresses" listing in the same year.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-184)
> "I have always tried to make life interesting for myself by doing different roles that connect mainstream cinema with its offbeat counterpart. I guess I have been daring and lucky with my roles. I want to do every kind of role with a reasonable amount of panache. I want to be a fair combination of style and substance"
—Matondkar on her approach to acting, during an interview in 2002.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Sukanya_Verma-185)

Title: Urmila Matondkar
Chunks: 21,22,23,24,25,26,27,32,33,34,35
In 2007, Matondkar appeared in an item song in Ram Gopal Varma's _Aag_[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-88) and was later seen in a cameo in the ensemble song "Deewangi Deewangi", in Farah Khan's _Om Shanti Om_.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-89) In the same year, she was seen in the action-thriller _Speed_ as part of an ensemble cast.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Speed_Movie_Review-90) Noting her reduced acting appearances during this phase, Taran Adarsh wrote in his review, "Urmila handles her part with dexterity and adds freshness to the goings-on since she has cut down on her acting assignments".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Speed_Movie_Review-90)
The next year, Matondkar appeared alongside Himesh Reshammiya in the thriller _Karzzzz_ (2008), a remake of the 1980 film _Karz_.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_in_Karzzzz_and_EMI-91) Her performance as Kamini (originally played by Simi Garewal) received praise, although the film was a critical and commercial failure.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-92) She also re-united with Sanjay Dutt for the social-comedy _EMI - Liya Hai Toh Chukana Padega!_ in the same year.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_in_Karzzzz_and_EMI-91)_EMI_ remains Matondkar's last leading role in Bollywood to date, although she continued to appear occasionally in films and television in the following years.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-93)

After a four-year absence from major film roles, Matondkar returned to films by voicing the character of Begum in the Hindi version of the animated musical comedy _Delhi Safari_, released in 2012.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-urmila-matondkar-comes-back-94) The same year, she made a special appearance in an item song in the Marathi film _Hridayanath_, starring Jackie Shroff. In 2013, she was seen in a cameo role in the adventure-comedy _Life Mein Hungama Hai_, which released after a delay of several years and went unnoticed.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-95)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_on_Dance_India_Dance_Super_Moms-8)
In 2014, Matondkar appeared in her first full-fledged role in Marathi cinema in the adventure-drama _Ajoba_.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-96) In the film, she portrayed Purva Rao, a wildlife activist in search of leopards. Praising her performance, _Daily News and Analysis_ wrote, "..this one's another jewel in her crown. She portrays Purva with a mild aggressive and rebellious streak. But all of these are an undercurrent to Purva's actions."[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-97)
Matondkar at a film screening in 2025.

In 2018, Matondkar ventured into film-production with the Marathi film _Madhuri_, as a co-producer along with her husband Mohsin Akhtar, under the banner _Mumbapuri Productions_.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_Matondkar_turns_producer-98) In the same year, she made a very brief return to Bollywood with a special appearance in the dark comedy _Blackmail_, in the song "Bewafa Beauty".[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-99)
In 2022, Matondkar was announced to star with Shreyas Talpade in a Marathi film titled _Tee Mee Navhech_. However, no significant updates on the project have been announced since.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-100)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-101) Later that year, she was announced to make her OTT debut with the action-thriller web series _Tiwari_, in which she plays the title role in a story centred on a mother and daughter.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-102) The series has subsequently faced post-production delays, and is unreleased as of 2026.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-103)
Matondkar has also been roped in for another upcoming IIT-based series produced by TVF, slated for release in mid-2027.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-104)

Alongside her film career, Matondkar has appeared as a celebrity guest on several reality television programmes, like _Movers & Shakers_, _Boogie Woogie_[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-105) and _The Manish Malhotra Show_. She also presented an episode of Sahara TV's _Dil Ki Baatein_ series in 2003, which featured Bollywood celebrities presenting vignettes from their personal lives.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-106)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-107).

In 2006, Matondkar was announced as a judge on Sahara One's reality show _Superstars_ alongside choreographer Shiamak Davar,[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-108)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-109)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-110) although the show was apparently shelved. However, a year later, she and Davar joined veteran actor Jeetendra as judges for the second season of Sony's dance reality show _Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa_.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Matondkar_on_Jhalak_Dikhla_Ja-111) Describing her experience of judging the show, Matondkar said, "I'm ecstatic about being able to be part of this show. I was facing the participants and audience for the first time. There were no written lines, no cues, no second chances. Either it worked or it didn't work for you. It was a concept that I liked."[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Matondkar_on_Jhalak_Dikhla_Ja-111) The next year, she hosted the singing reality show _Waar Parriwar_ on the same channel.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-112) She mentioned in an interview that she agreed to host the show because she felt comfortable with its family-oriented format, and also emphasized her preference for authenticity over scripted drama in reality TV.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-113)
Matondkar on the sets of _Chak Dhoom Dhoom season 2_ in 2011.

In 2011, she was roped in for the second season of Colors' dance reality show _Chak Dhoom Dhoom_.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-urmila-matondkar-comes-back-94) She replaced Mallika Sherawat, and joined Javed Jaffrey and Terence Lewis in the judging panel.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-114)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-115) Matondkar subsequently ventured into Marathi television, with Zee Marathi's dance reality show _Marathi Paaul Padte Pudhe_ (2011–2012), where she served as a judge in its second season.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-116) She then featured as the 'Grand Master' judge in _Dance Maharashtra Dance_ (2012–2013), on the same channel.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-117)
After ten years, Matondkar returned to Hindi television with the third season of _DID Super Moms_ (2022), on Zee TV.

She featured as a co-judge alongside [Remo D'Souza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remo_D'Souza "Remo D'Souza") and Bhagyashree.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_Matondkar_defends_projection_of_contestants'_sob_stories-118)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_on_Dance_India_Dance_Super_Moms-8) In an interview for the show, she supported the inclusion of personal backstories of the contestants on reality television, stating that it was important for audiences to understand their journeys and struggles.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila_Matondkar_defends_projection_of_contestants'_sob_stories-118) Matondkar continues to make occasional appearances as a guest in shows like _Indian Idol_,[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-119)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-120)_Sa Re Ga Ma Pa_,[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-121)_Dance Deewane_,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-122)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-123)_Zee Comedy Show_,[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-124)_Khupte Tithe Gupte_[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-125) and _[India's Best Dancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India's\_Best\_Dancer\_(Hindi\_TV\_series) "India's Best Dancer (Hindi TV series)")_.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-126)

In 2004, Matondkar featured in the music video of the song "Deewanay", by the Pakistani pop-rock band Fuzön, directed by Prahlad Kakkar and Saqib Malik.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-164)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-165) The collaboration aimed at promoting India–Pakistan peace and cultural exchange, drawing major media attention when she visited Lahore to shoot the video.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-166) In 2007, Matondkar marked a rare venture into singing by lending her vocals to the song "Mehbooba Dilruba", for Asha Bhonsle's music album _Asha & Friends Vol. 1_, and also appeared in the accompanying video of the song with Bhonsle.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-167)[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-168)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-169)
[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shabana,_Urmila_and_Dia_supporting_Anna_Hazare's_movement.jpg)
Matondkar in a rally for Anna Hazare's movement, alongside Shabana Azmi and Dia Mirza, in 2011.
Prior to entering active politics, Matondkar was associated with various charitable initiatives and has particularly supported causes related to the empowerment of women in India. She was among several film personalities who rallied in support of Anna Hazare's anti-corruption movement in 2011 in Mumbai.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-170)

Matondkar officially joined the Indian National Congress on 27 March 2019.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-171) She stated in an interview that she had been approached for political roles earlier in her career too, but had chosen to decline them before eventually entering politics due to socio-political concerns.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-172) She contested from Mumbai North constituency in the 2019 Lok Sabha Election.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-173) She lost out to Gopal Shetty of the Bhartiya Janta Party, who retained the seat by a massive margin of over 4 lakhs votes.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-174) She resigned from the party on 10 September 2019 by submitting her writing to Sonia Gandhi (then interim chief of the Congress), and cited "petty in-house politics" as a reason behind her resignation.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-175)
On 1 December 2020, Matondkar joined the Shiv Sena in presence of party president Uddhav Thackeray.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Quint2020-176)[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-177) Shiv Sena hoped to add a nationally recognised face and voice, well conversant in Marathi, Hindi as well as English, to represent the party.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Quint2020-176) In 2022, she participated in _Bharat Jodo Yatra_, joining Rahul Gandhi during the march, despite having earlier left the Congress.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-178)

Matondkar has been described by critics as one of the most talented actresses of Indian cinema and has also been praised for her dancing skills.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-179)[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Urmila's_best_dance_sequences-180)_The Tribune_ described her as a versatile actress and a "glam doll" who successfully transitioned from child artist roles to a leading performer.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Glamdoll-2001-181) Following the success of _Rangeela_ (1995), media coverage frequently described Matondkar as a "sex symbol" of contemporary Hindi cinema, a label that she acknowledged as being shaped largely by publicity and promotional framing, which contributed to her being typecast.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Srinivasan,_V_S-5) She was included in _The Tribune_'s list of Bollywood's top five actresses of 1998.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Top-5-actresses-1998-182)
Matondkar in 2010

By the early 2000s, publications such as _Rediff_ noted that she had moved beyond the early "glamour" label, establishing herself through varied and often unconventional roles in films such as _Kaun?_, _Bhoot_, and _Pinjar_. Because she could go from being the ultimate glamour girl to being completely de-glammed and terrified in a dark apartment, the film press in that era often described her as "The Goddess" — someone who could hold audience with just her eyes, whether she was dancing or in complete silence. In a 2003 feature interview in _The Tribune_, Matondkar was described as an established actress whose career included both commercial films and roles across varied genres.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-TribuneSpectrum-183) She featured in _Rediff'_ s "Top Bollywood Actresses" listing in the same year.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-184)
> "I have always tried to make life interesting for myself by doing different roles that connect mainstream cinema with its offbeat counterpart. I guess I have been daring and lucky with my roles. I want to do every kind of role with a reasonable amount of panache. I want to be a fair combination of style and substance"
—Matondkar on her approach to acting, during an interview in 2002.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar#cite_note-Sukanya_Verma-185)

Title: From Child Star to South Cinema Queen: Hansika Motwani’s Remarkable Journey

Hansika Motwani began her career as a child artist in Hindi films before rising to stardom in Tamil and Telugu cinema. She won widespread acclaim with lead roles in blockbuster Telugu films like Desamuduru, Kantri, and Maska. Today, Hansika remains one of the most popular and admired actresses in South Indian cinema.
